# Terraform Refactor: Duplicated dev/prod → One Module with `for_each`

## Before (problem)

```hcl
# main.tf — duplicated blocks
module "eks_dev"  { source = "./modules/eks"  instance_types = ["t3.medium"] desired_size = 2 ... }
module "eks_prod" { source = "./modules/eks"  instance_types = ["t3.large"]  desired_size = 4 ... }
module "bucket_dev"  { ... }
module "bucket_prod" { ... replication = true }
module "rds_dev"  { instance_class = "db.t3.micro" multi_az = false ... }
module "rds_prod" { instance_class = "db.t3.medium" multi_az = true ... }
# ... same for IAM, CloudFront, secrets
```

## After

### Directory layout

```
envs/
  main.tf          # for_each over env map
  envs.tf          # environment config map
  dev.tfvars
  prod.tfvars
modules/
  environment/     # one environment's full topology
    main.tf
    eks.tf
    s3.tf
    rds.tf
    iam.tf
    https.tf
    secrets.tf
    variables.tf
```

### `envs/envs.tf`

```hcl
variable "environment" {
  description = "Target environment"
  type        = string
  validation {
    condition     = contains(["dev", "prod"], var.environment)
    error_message = "environment must be dev or prod."
  }
}

locals {
  envs = {
    dev = {
      region             = "us-east-1"
      replica_region     = null # no replication
      node_instance_type = "t3.medium"
      node_count         = 2
      db_instance_class  = "db.t3.micro"
      db_multi_az        = false
      db_encrypted       = true
      is_prod            = false
    }
    prod = {
      region             = "us-east-1"
      replica_region     = "us-west-2"
      node_instance_type = "t3.large"
      node_count         = 4
      db_instance_class  = "db.t3.medium"
      db_multi_az        = true
      db_encrypted       = true
      is_prod            = true
    }
  }
  env = local.envs[var.environment]
}
```

### `envs/main.tf`

```hcl
module "environment" {
  source   = "../modules/environment"
  for_each = toset([var.environment])

  name               = each.key
  region             = local.env.region
  replica_region     = local.env.replica_region
  node_instance_type = local.env.node_instance_type
  node_count         = local.env.node_count
  db_instance_class  = local.env.db_instance_class
  db_multi_az        = local.env.db_multi_az
  db_encrypted       = local.env.db_encrypted
  is_prod            = local.env.is_prod

  db_secret = sensitive(var.db_connection_string) # via -var-file with SOPS-decrypted tfvars
}
```

> **Note:** `for_each` here gives you the module-instance indirection needed for state moves while keeping per-env tfvars isolation. If you use **workspaces** instead, drop the tfvars files and key off `terraform.workspace` — but the `moved` blocks below are identical.

### `modules/environment/rds.tf` (representative)

```hcl
resource "aws_db_instance" "this" {
  identifier             = "${var.name}-db"
  engine                 = "postgres"
  instance_class         = var.db_instance_class
  multi_az               = var.db_multi_az
  storage_encrypted      = var.db_encrypted
  deletion_protection    = true
  backup_retention_period = 7
  publicly_accessible    = false
  username               = "app"
  password               = var.db_secret
}
```

`iam.tf` uses a conditional least-privilege policy (wildcard actions only when `!var.is_prod`); `s3.tf` uses `dynamic "replication_configuration"` when `var.replica_region != null`.

## Zero-diff state moves

Add `moved` blocks (Terraform ≥ 1.1 — no CLI `state mv` surgery, works in CI). Keys depend on your old addresses:

```hcl
moved {
  from = module.eks_dev
  to   = module.environment["dev"].module.eks
}
moved {
  from = module.rds_dev.aws_db_instance.this
  to   = module.environment["dev"].aws_db_instance.this
}
moved {
  from = module.bucket_prod.aws_s3_bucket.this
  to   = module.environment["prod"].aws_s3_bucket.this
}
# ... one moved block per old resource address → new address
```

### Verification procedure

```bash
terraform init
terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev.tfvars -out=dev.tfplan   # expect: "Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy"
terraform plan -var-file=envs/prod.tfvars -out=prod.tfplan # same
```

If any diff appears, the old address in the `moved` block is wrong — fix it, don't ignore it.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

| # | How satisfied |
|---|---|
| 1 | S3 module: versioning, SSE, `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` always on |
| 2 | RDS: `deletion_protection`, `backup_retention_period = 7`, `publicly_accessible = false` (both envs) |
| 3 | DB secret via SOPS-encrypted tfvars (`sops -d dev.tfvars.enc > /tmp/dev.tfvars`) or `carlpett/sops` provider; never committed plaintext |
| 4 | Prod policy has no `"*"` actions (enforced by `is_prod` conditional + a `check`/policy test) |
| 5 | Managed node group with env-specific type/count from `locals.envs` |
| 6 | ALB/CloudFront HTTPS listener only, ACM cert ARN reference |
| 7 | Separate state per env (workspaces or `-var-file` + separate backends keys), `for_each` keyed on the single env so only one instance exists per apply |

## Rollback safety

`moved` blocks are declarative and idempotent; to roll back, revert the refactor commit — Terraform replays the moves in reverse with zero-diff. Keep the moved blocks in-tree permanently (they're cheap and make the migration auditable in VCS).
